# dsh-egress-gate
> **If this helps you, please give it a star** — it helps others find it. Thanks!

Deterministic network egress gate for
DeepSeek Harness (dsh).

Content scanning (dsh-read-guard) guards what **enters** the model; this
guards where data may **lea

ve** to. `web_fetch` / `web_search` calls are
checked against a destination allowlist in `tools/pre-

execute` and denied
before they run. Shell commands are scanned for fetch-verb URLs —
observation by

default, enforcement opt-in, honest about precision. Zero LLM
calls in the trust path.

Family: read · write · do · call · leave-behind · **egress (where data may
flow)**.
## Why now (checked 2026-10-12)

Empty lane. Five keyword searches (`network allowlist`, `egress firewall`,
`url filter`, `web fetch

restrict`, …) return nothing on GitHub; the awesome
list has no entry gating destinations. Neighbour

s are all different axes:
content-pattern secret rules (dsh-defend), LLM-judged commands
(dsh-jev-gu

ard), proxy *configuration* (official network-proxy docs). For
teams, "which hosts may the agent rea

ch" is the first compliance question —
and the deterministic answer was unowned.
## Policy

- Deny always wins; a non-empty `allow` list means "only these hosts"
(`example.com` covers `api.exa

mple.com`; `*.example.com` is the explicit
form).
- Web tools are enforced at full precision — the U

RL is in the arguments.
- Shell: URLs following `curl` / `wget` / `Invoke-WebRequest` /
`Invoke-Rest

Method` / `fetch` / `http` on the same command segment. This
cannot see through scripts, variables,

or proxies — so it warns by
default and denies only when you opt into `shellMode: 'enforce'`.

## Compatibility
- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile

via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/

24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fr
esh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-egress-gate` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-egress-gate] acti
ve: …`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-egress-gate` → dependencies cleared, bundles restor
…`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-egress-gate` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.
## Develop
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Kill criteria

If dsh ships first-party destination policy, or proxy-layer plugins add
per-host rules, this freezes

at its last working version with a postmortem
here.
## Known limitations
- **Web tools are enforced; shell is observe-only by default** (set `shellMode: 'enforce'` to change
). A fetch verb gates every URL in its own command segment; segments without one (a plain echo) are

not treated as sends.
- **No redirect resolution**: the check sees the requested host, not where a r

edirect lands.
- **This is not an OS-level network control.** Scripts, sockets, proxies, and MCP too
ls with their own network access are outside this gate — use a sandbox or proxy for hard boundaries.
